topics.title: Singing

qs.q: Do you like singing? / Do you often sing? / When do you like to sing?
qs.a6: Yes, I do, but I'm not a good singer. I sing in the bathroom or when I'm cleaning my room. Sometimes I sing karaoke with friends.
qs.a7: Yes, I do, although I wouldn't say I'm a talented singer. I mostly sing in the shower or while I'm tidying up, and now and then I go to karaoke with friends to let off some steam.

qs.q: What kinds of music do you like to sing? / Do you sing in the car?
qs.a6: I like slow pop songs and ballads because they are easy to sing. I don't have a car, but on the bus I sing quietly in my head.
qs.a7: I'm into slow pop songs and ballads, as they're easy on the voice. I don't drive, but on the bus I sometimes hum along to the music in my headphones.

qs.q: Have you ever learnt how to sing? / Did you take music lessons? / Does your school teach singing?
qs.a6: No, I never took singing lessons. At primary school we had music classes, and we sang some simple songs together. But I never learnt it seriously.
qs.a7: Not formally. We had music lessons at primary school where we sang simple songs in groups, but I've never had any proper training.

qs.q: Do you like listening to other people sing? / Do many people in Vietnam know how to sing?
qs.a6: Yes, I enjoy it, especially live singing. Many Vietnamese people love singing, and karaoke is very popular, so a lot of people can sing a little.
qs.a7: Yes, particularly live performances. Singing is a big part of Vietnamese culture, and karaoke is hugely popular, so most people can carry a tune, at least roughly.

qs.q: Do you think singing can bring happiness to people?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. When people sing, they forget their stress and feel more relaxed. Singing together also makes people closer.
qs.a7: Definitely. Singing is a great stress-reliever, and singing together with friends or family really strengthens the bond between people.

qs.q: Did you enjoy singing when you were younger?
qs.a6: Yes, I did. I often sang with my friends at school and at family parties.
qs.a7: Yes, quite a lot. I used to sing along with my friends at school and at family gatherings.

qs.q: Who do you want to sing for?
qs.a6: I want to sing for my family and close friends, because they are kind and they don't care if I sing badly.
qs.a7: For my family and close friends, as they're supportive and never judge my voice.

qs.q: How well did you sing?
qs.a6: Not very well. My voice is average, but I can sing in tune with easy songs.
qs.a7: Nothing special. My voice is average, though I can carry a tune on simple songs.

topics.title: The area you live in

qs.q: Do you like the area that you live in? / Which town or city do you live in now?
qs.a6: I live in the suburbs of Hanoi, and I like it. It's quiet and less crowded than the city centre, and the air is better.
qs.a7: I live on the outskirts of Hanoi, and I'm quite fond of it. It's much quieter and less congested than the centre, and the air feels fresher.

qs.q: Are there any things you don't like about your area? / What are some changes in the area recently?
qs.a6: The main problem is the traffic jam in rush hour and the lack of buses at night. Recently, the road has been widened and a new supermarket has opened, so life is more convenient.
qs.a7: My main gripe is the rush-hour congestion and the lack of evening buses. On the plus side, the main road has recently been widened and a new supermarket has opened, which has made life more convenient.

qs.q: Do you know your neighbours? / Are the people in your neighbourhood friendly?
qs.a6: Yes, I know many of them because we have lived there for a long time. They are friendly, and they often say hello and help each other.
qs.a7: I know quite a few of them, since we've lived there for years. They're warm and neighbourly, and we look out for one another.

qs.q: Do you live in a house or an apartment? / What is your favourite room?
qs.a6: I live in a three-storey house with my parents and my younger brother. My favourite room is my bedroom because it's quiet and I can relax or study there.
qs.a7: I live in a three-storey house with my parents and younger brother. My favourite room is my bedroom, as it's my little sanctuary where I can unwind or study in peace.

qs.q: Do you think you will continue to live there for a long time? / Do you like living in the countryside?
qs.a6: Probably yes, because my family is there. But if I have a better job, I may move closer to the city. I like the countryside for holidays, but I need the city for work.
qs.a7: Probably, as my family is there, though I might move closer to the centre if my career takes off. I love the countryside for short breaks, but the city suits my work better.

qs.q: Where do you like to go in that area?
qs.a6: I like going to the small park and a café near my house. They are quiet and good for relaxing.
qs.a7: A small park and a cosy café nearby, which are both peaceful places to unwind.

qs.q: Do you know any famous people in your area?
qs.a6: Not really. I only know a local singer who lives in the next village, but I have never met him.
qs.a7: Not really. A local singer lives in the next village, but I've never met him.

qs.q: What things make your home pleasant to live in?
qs.a6: My family, the quiet space and the fresh air. Also the roof terrace with my mother's plants.
qs.a7: My family, the peaceful surroundings, the fresh air and my mother's roof garden.

topics.title: Science

qs.q: Did you like studying science at school? / What is your favourite science subject?
qs.a6: Yes, I liked it, especially physics and maths. I like to understand how things work, and the experiments were interesting.
qs.a7: Yes, particularly physics, because I enjoyed figuring out how things work, and the experiments made lessons more engaging.

qs.q: What do you remember about your science teachers?
qs.a6: I remember my physics teacher. He was funny and patient, and he often used simple experiments to explain difficult ideas.
qs.a7: I remember my physics teacher vividly. He was witty and patient, and he often used simple experiments to make complex ideas easy to grasp.

qs.q: How interested are you in science now? / How do you learn about science in daily life?
qs.a6: I'm quite interested, especially in technology because of my job. I read news and watch videos on YouTube about new inventions.
qs.a7: Quite interested, particularly in technology, given my line of work. I keep up with new inventions through articles and YouTube videos.

qs.q: What do you think has been an important recent scientific development? / Is there any technology that is helpful in daily life?
qs.a6: I think artificial intelligence is very important. It helps us write, translate and find information faster. Smartphones are also very useful in daily life.
qs.a7: I'd say artificial intelligence, which is transforming how we work, translate and look things up. Smartphones are another game-changer in everyday life.

qs.q: Do you think everyone should study science at school? / Are science classes important?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. Science teaches us to think logically and helps us understand the world, for example health and the environment.
qs.a7: Yes, it teaches logical thinking and helps people make informed decisions about health and the environment, so it should be part of everyone's education.

qs.q: When did you start to learn science?
qs.a6: I started in primary school, when I was about eight years old.
qs.a7: In primary school, at around the age of eight.

qs.q: Did you study / learn much science at primary school?
qs.a6: Only the basics, like plants, animals and the human body. We learned more in secondary school.
qs.a7: Just the basics, such as plants, animals and the human body; the real learning came in secondary school.

qs.q: How does knowing about science help you in your everyday life?
qs.a6: It helps me to understand things like electricity, health and food, so I can make safer choices. It also helps me with my IT job.
qs.a7: It helps me understand electricity, health and nutrition so I can make informed choices, and it underpins my IT work.

topics.title: Memory

qs.q: Are you good at memorising things? / Do you need to remember things often?
qs.a6: Not really. I need to remember many things at work, like tasks and bug numbers, so I write them down.
qs.a7: Not particularly. My job involves a lot of details, such as task lists and bug IDs, so I rely on notes rather than my memory.

qs.q: How do you remember important things? / Why do more people rely on cell phones to memorise things?
qs.a6: I use the notes app and set alarms on my phone. Many people use phones because it's easy and fast, and they don't need to remember anything.
qs.a7: I use a notes app and set reminders. People lean on phones because they're convenient and reliable, so there's less need to memorise anything.

qs.q: Have you ever forgotten something important?
qs.a6: Yes, once I forgot a deadline at work. I felt very worried, so I worked late to finish. Since then I always set a reminder.
qs.a7: Yes, I once forgot a deadline at work and had to stay late to make up for it. Ever since, I've set reminders for everything important.

qs.q: Is it easy to remember people's names? / Why do some people have good memories?
qs.a6: No, I find it hard to remember names, especially when I meet many people. Some people have good memories because they practise or sleep well, or maybe it's natural.
qs.a7: Not at all. Names slip my mind, particularly when I meet lots of people at once. Some have better memories thanks to genes, healthy sleep and regular mental exercise.

qs.q: Would you like to have a better memory?
qs.a6: Yes, of course. A better memory would help me study English vocabulary faster and work more efficiently.
qs.a7: Definitely. A sharper memory would help me pick up English vocabulary faster and be more productive at work.

qs.q: What do you need to remember in your daily life?
qs.a6: Work tasks, meetings, passwords, bus times and my family's birthdays.
qs.a7: Work tasks, meetings, passwords, bus schedules and family birthdays.

qs.q: Do you remember things easily when studying or working?
qs.a6: It depends. I remember better when I write notes or learn in the morning. Long lists are hard for me.
qs.a7: It depends. I retain more when I take notes or study in the morning, but long lists are a struggle.

topics.title: Work

qs.q: Are you a student or do you work now? / What work do you do?
qs.a6: I work. I'm a software tester at an IT company in Hanoi. I check the software and find bugs before it goes to customers.
qs.a7: I work as a software tester at an IT company in Hanoi. My job is to check applications for bugs before they reach customers.

qs.q: Why did you choose that type of work? / What requirements did you need to meet?
qs.a6: I studied IT at university, and I like checking details, so testing suits me. To get the job, I needed a degree and some basic knowledge of testing.
qs.a7: I studied IT, and I have an eye for detail, so testing was a natural fit. The requirements were a relevant degree and basic testing knowledge.

qs.q: Do you like your job? / What do you like best about it?
qs.a6: Yes, I do. I like solving problems and working with a team. Sometimes it's stressful near deadlines, but I learn a lot.
qs.a7: Yes, for the most part. I enjoy problem-solving and teamwork, and although deadlines can be stressful, I'm learning constantly.

qs.q: What technology do you use at work? / Who helps you the most?
qs.a6: I use a computer, test tools and a bug management tool. My manager and my senior colleagues help me the most. They explain things patiently.
qs.a7: I use test management and bug-tracking tools every day. My manager and senior colleagues support me the most, always explaining things patiently.

qs.q: Do you have any plans for your work in the next five years? / Do you want to change to another job?
qs.a6: In five years, I want to be an automation tester or a team leader. I don't want to change my job now, but I'm improving my English for better chances.
qs.a7: Within five years, I'd like to move into automation or team leadership. I'm not looking to switch jobs just yet, but I'm working on my English to open more doors.

qs.q: Which is more important to you: the people you work with or the work you do?
qs.a6: For me, the people are more important. If colleagues are friendly, I feel happy and I can work better.
qs.a7: The people, I'd say. With supportive colleagues, even a demanding job feels manageable.

qs.q: What would you like to do in the future?
qs.a6: I'd like to become an automation tester and later a team leader.
qs.a7: I'd like to move into test automation and eventually lead a team.

qs.q: What are the benefits of being your age?
qs.a6: I have energy, I can learn fast and I have time to try new things.
qs.a7: I have plenty of energy, learn quickly and have time to experiment before settling down.

qs.q: What do you think is the most important at the moment?
qs.a6: Improving my English and my skills, because they decide my future career.
qs.a7: Improving my English and technical skills, as they'll shape my career.

qs.q: Do you prefer to work in the morning or afternoon?
qs.a6: In the morning, because my mind is fresh. In the afternoon I feel sleepy after lunch.
qs.a7: Mornings, when my mind is sharp; I tend to get sleepy after lunch.

qs.q: Have you changed your work before?
qs.a6: Yes, once. I started as a part-time intern and then changed to a full-time tester at another company.
qs.a7: Once. I began as an intern and then moved to a full-time tester role at another company.

topics.title: Study

qs.q: What do you study? / Why did you choose that subject?
qs.a6: I studied Information Technology at university. I chose it because I like computers and the job market is good. Now I'm studying English by myself for IELTS.
qs.a7: I studied Information Technology because I'm fascinated by computers and the job prospects are good. These days I'm self-studying English for IELTS.

qs.q: Do you study best in the morning or the afternoon? / How much time do you spend studying every week?
qs.a6: I study best in the morning because my head is clear. I spend about six to eight hours a week, because I work during the day.
qs.a7: I'm sharpest in the morning, when my mind is clear. I manage about six to eight hours a week around my work schedule.

qs.q: What technology do you use when you study?
qs.a6: I use my phone and laptop. I use apps, YouTube and online dictionaries, and I record my voice to practise speaking.
qs.a7: My phone and laptop, mainly. I rely on learning apps, YouTube and online dictionaries, and I record myself to practise speaking.

qs.q: Do you think your subject is popular in your country? / What are the most popular subjects in Vietnam?
qs.a6: Yes, IT is very popular, because jobs are well paid. Other popular subjects are business, economics and medicine.
qs.a7: Yes, IT is hugely popular thanks to lucrative career prospects, along with business, economics and medicine.

qs.q: Do you think it's important to choose a subject you like? / Do you miss being a student?
qs.a6: Yes, because you will study with more motivation. I sometimes miss being a student because I had more free time and friends around me.
qs.a7: Absolutely, since passion fuels motivation. I do miss student life occasionally, for the free time and the friends around me.

qs.q: Which study / subject is the most interesting?
qs.a6: Programming and software testing, because I can use them to solve real problems.
qs.a7: Programming and testing, since I can apply them to real problems.

qs.q: Teachers or other students: which is more important?
qs.a6: The teachers, because they guide us. But classmates also help by sharing ideas.
qs.a7: Teachers, as they provide guidance, though classmates help by sharing ideas.

qs.q: How do you usually travel to the city where you study?
qs.a6: I take the bus because it's cheap, and it takes about one hour.
qs.a7: By bus, which is cheap, taking around an hour.

qs.q: Have you always wanted to study this subject?
qs.a6: Not always. At first, I just liked computers. Then I knew IT jobs are good, so I chose it.
qs.a7: Not always. I started out simply liking computers, then realised IT offered good career prospects.

qs.q: Plans for your studies in the next five years?
qs.a6: I plan to get IELTS 6.5 and the ISTQB certificate, and learn more programming.
qs.a7: To achieve IELTS 6.5, earn the ISTQB certificate and deepen my programming skills.

qs.q: Do you want to change your major?
qs.a6: No, I'm happy with IT, but I'd like to add business knowledge.
qs.a7: No, I'm happy with IT, though I'd like to add some business knowledge.

qs.q: What changes would you like to see in your school?
qs.a6: More practical lessons and better English teaching, and modern equipment.
qs.a7: More hands-on lessons, stronger English teaching and modern equipment.

qs.q: Are you looking forward to working?
qs.a6: I am already working, and yes, I look forward to a better position.
qs.a7: I'm already working, and I'm looking forward to growing into a more senior role.

topics.note: Lưu ý: với "Study" (Topic 6), bạn đang đi làm nên mình trả lời theo hướng "tôi đã tốt nghiệp ngành IT" và "bây giờ tôi tự học tiếng Anh". Nếu giám khảo hỏi "Are you a student or do you work?" bạn nói là đi làm.

topics.title: Teachers

qs.q: Do you have a favourite teacher? / Who was your favourite teacher in elementary school?
qs.a6: Yes, my primary school teacher, Mrs Lan. She was kind and patient, and she taught me to read and write well.
qs.a7: Yes, my primary school teacher, Mrs Lan. She was kind and endlessly patient, and she gave me a solid foundation in reading and writing.

qs.q: How has she/he helped you?
qs.a6: She helped me to love studying. When I made mistakes, she didn't get angry. She encouraged me to try again.
qs.a7: She sparked my love of learning. When I made mistakes, she never scolded me but encouraged me to try again.

qs.q: Do you still keep in touch with your former teachers?
qs.a6: Yes, with some of them. I visit my primary school teacher on Teachers' Day, and I send messages on Zalo to my university teacher.
qs.a7: With a few of them. I visit my primary teacher around Teachers' Day and occasionally message a university lecturer on Zalo.

qs.q: Do you think teachers are different now than when your parents were at school?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. Teachers now use technology like projectors and online classes, and they are more friendly with students. In my parents' time, teachers were stricter.
qs.a7: Yes, they are. Today's teachers use technology such as projectors and online classes and are more approachable, whereas in my parents' day they were much stricter.

qs.q: Do you think you could be a teacher? / Did you want to be a teacher when you were young?
qs.a6: No, I don't think so. I'm not patient enough and I'm shy when speaking in front of many people. But I like to explain things to my colleagues.
qs.a7: Probably not. I lack the patience and I get shy in front of large groups, although I do enjoy explaining things to colleagues.

qs.q: Do you remember one of your teachers? Is it easy to remember elementary school teachers?
qs.a6: Yes, I remember Mrs Lan very well, because she was kind. I also remember my maths teacher. It's easy to remember teachers who were special to us.
qs.a7: Yes, vividly: Mrs Lan, for her kindness. Teachers who left a strong impression are easy to remember.

qs.q: What were your primary school teachers like?
qs.a6: They were kind, patient and gentle. They often used songs and games to teach.
qs.a7: Kind, gentle and patient, and they used songs and games to keep us engaged.

qs.q: Which teacher do you prefer, primary or junior high?
qs.a6: Primary school teachers, because they were closer to us and more caring. Junior high teachers were stricter.
qs.a7: Primary teachers, as they were more caring, while junior high ones were stricter.

topics.title: Social media

qs.q: Do you think you spend too much time on social media? / When did you start using it?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. I started using Facebook when I was in high school. Now I spend about two hours a day, and it's too much.
qs.a7: I'm afraid so. I joined Facebook in high school, and now I spend around two hours a day on it, which is more than I'd like.

qs.q: What do people often do on social media? / Do you like to use it?
qs.a6: People watch short videos, chat with friends, share photos and read news. I like it for entertainment, but it wastes time.
qs.a7: People watch short videos, chat, share photos and catch up on news. I enjoy it for entertainment, although it can be a real time-waster.

qs.q: Do your friends use social media too much?
qs.a6: Yes, some of them do. They check their phones all the time, even when we eat together.
qs.a7: Some of them do. They're glued to their phones, even when we're having a meal together.

qs.q: What's the most popular social media in Vietnam? Why?
qs.a6: Facebook, Zalo and TikTok are the most popular. Facebook and Zalo are good for chatting and work groups, and TikTok has fun short videos.
qs.a7: Facebook, Zalo and TikTok. Facebook and Zalo are handy for chatting and work groups, while TikTok's short videos are very addictive.

qs.q: Do you want to work in social media? / Do people find social media useful?
qs.a6: No, I prefer my job. But I think people find it useful because they can keep in touch and sell things online.
qs.a7: Not really, I'm happy in IT. But most people find it useful for staying connected and even for running small businesses.

topics.title: Dream and ambition

qs.q: What was your childhood dream? / What was your dream job when you were young?
qs.a6: When I was a child, I wanted to be a police officer because I thought the uniform was cool and the job was brave.
qs.a7: As a kid, I dreamt of becoming a police officer, since I thought the uniform looked cool and the job seemed heroic.

qs.q: Have you changed your mind on your dream job? / What is your dream job?
qs.a6: Yes, I have. Now I want to be a senior automation tester or a QA lead. It's more realistic and it matches my skills.
qs.a7: Yes. These days my dream job is a QA lead, which is far more realistic and plays to my strengths.

qs.q: Do you think you are an ambitious person? / Are you the kind of person who sticks to dreams?
qs.a6: I think I'm moderately ambitious. I have clear goals, like improving my English, but I'm not the type to take big risks. I usually stick to my goals once I start.
qs.a7: Moderately so. I set clear goals, such as improving my English, though I'm not a big risk-taker. Once I commit, I tend to stick with it.

qs.q: Do you have any dreams or hopes for your life?
qs.a6: Yes. I hope to have a stable job, a happy family and enough money to take care of my parents. I also want to travel more.
qs.a7: Yes: a secure career, a happy family and the means to look after my parents. I'd also love to travel more.

topics.title: Outer space and stars

qs.q: Have you ever learned about outer space and stars? / Did you learn about space at school?
qs.a6: Yes, a little. We learned about the solar system in geography and science classes. I remember the planets and the moon.
qs.a7: A little. We covered the solar system in school, and I still remember the order of the planets.

qs.q: Do you enjoy films about outer space? / Do you like science-fiction movies set in space?
qs.a6: Yes, I like them because the pictures are beautiful and the stories are exciting. I like science fiction films very much.
qs.a7: Yes, I'm a fan. The visuals are stunning and the stories are gripping, so science fiction is one of my favourite genres.

qs.q: Do you want to go into outer space in the future? What would you do?
qs.a6: I think it would be exciting, but I'm a bit afraid. If I had the chance, I would look at the Earth from space and take photos.
qs.a7: It'd be thrilling, though a bit scary. If I got the chance, I'd gaze back at Earth from space and take plenty of photos.

qs.q: Is it important to study stars? / Do you want to know more about outer space?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. Studying space helps us understand the universe and develops new technology. I'd like to know more, but I'm too busy.
qs.a7: Yes, it expands our knowledge of the universe and drives technological progress. I'd love to learn more, time permitting.

qs.q: Do you learn about outer space and arts at school?
qs.a6: We learned a little about space in science, and art lessons were separate. I liked drawing the planets.
qs.a7: A little space in science class, with art as a separate subject; I enjoyed drawing the planets.

qs.q: Have you ever taken a course about stars?
qs.a6: No, I haven't. But I watched some online videos about stars and the universe.
qs.a7: No, never, though I've watched online videos about stars and the universe.

topics.note: Thông tin giả định theo hồ sơ: IT Tester, thích chăm sóc bản thân, ngoại hình. Bạn sửa chi tiết khi nói rồi gửi mình chấm.

topics.title: Clothing

qs.q: Do you prefer to wear comfortable, casual clothes or smart clothes?
qs.a6: I prefer comfortable clothes, like T-shirts and jeans. At work, I can dress casually, but for important meetings I wear a shirt.
qs.a7: Comfortable, casual clothes like T-shirts and jeans, as my office has a relaxed dress code, although I smarten up for important meetings.

qs.q: Do you spend a lot of time choosing clothes? / Are you a fashionable person?
qs.a6: Yes, a little. I like to look neat and clean, so I check my outfit in the morning. I'm not very fashionable, but I like simple, nice clothes.
qs.a7: A fair amount. I care about looking neat, so I take a few minutes to pick an outfit. I'm not exactly a fashionista, but I like clean, simple styles.

qs.q: Do you wear different clothes on the weekend?
qs.a6: Yes. On weekends, I wear more relaxed clothes, like shorts or a hoodie. When I go out with friends, I choose something nicer.
qs.a7: Yes, something more laid-back such as shorts or a hoodie, though I dress up a little when I'm meeting friends.

qs.q: Do you like wearing T-shirts? / What kind of clothes do you like to wear?
qs.a6: Yes, I do. T-shirts are comfortable, cheap and easy to wear. I like white and dark blue because they are easy to match.
qs.a7: Yes, they're comfortable, affordable and versatile. I tend to go for white and navy, since they're easy to mix and match.

topics.title: Mirrors

qs.q: How often do you use a mirror? / Do you like looking at yourself in the mirror?
qs.a6: I use a mirror every morning and evening, when I wash my face and do my skincare. I like looking at myself to check my skin and my hair.
qs.a7: Several times a day, in fact, mainly during my morning and evening skincare routine. I like to check my skin and hair before heading out.

qs.q: Do you usually take a mirror with you?
qs.a6: Not usually. But I use the camera on my phone like a mirror when I need to check my face.
qs.a7: Not as a rule, though I'll use my phone's front camera in a pinch.

qs.q: Do you use a mirror before buying clothing? / Have you ever bought mirrors?
qs.a6: Yes, I always use the mirror in the fitting room to see if the clothes fit. I once bought a big mirror for my room because it makes the room brighter.
qs.a7: Always. I check the fit in the fitting-room mirror. I once bought a large mirror for my bedroom, which makes the room look brighter and more spacious.

qs.q: What functions does a mirror have? / Is a mirror a good decoration?
qs.a6: A mirror helps us check our look. It can also make a small room look bigger. I think it's a good decoration if it has a nice frame.
qs.a7: Beyond checking our appearance, mirrors make small rooms feel larger and reflect natural light. A mirror with an attractive frame also works as stylish décor.

qs.q: Would you use mirrors to decorate your room?
qs.a6: Yes. A big mirror makes a small room look bigger and brighter, so I use one in my bedroom.
qs.a7: Yes. A large mirror makes a small room feel bigger and brighter, and I have one in my bedroom.

topics.note: Thông tin giả định theo hồ sơ: IT Tester, thích chăm sóc bản thân, ngoại hình. Bạn sửa chi tiết khi nói rồi gửi mình chấm.

topics.title: Free time & weekend

qs.q: What do you usually do in your spare time? / What do you enjoy doing most on weekends?
qs.a6: I usually watch films, listen to music and meet friends for coffee. Sometimes I read books or study English. On weekends, I like to sleep a bit longer and relax.
qs.a7: I mostly watch films, listen to music and meet friends over coffee, with a bit of reading and English study in between. At weekends, I enjoy a lie-in and a slow start.

qs.q: Do you like going to the cinema at weekends? Who do you go with?
qs.a6: Yes, sometimes. I usually go with friends or my brother, because it's more fun to share the film. I like action and science fiction movies.
qs.a7: Now and then. I usually go with friends or my brother, since sharing a film is half the fun. I love action and sci-fi.

qs.q: How do you often relax on weekends? / Which day do you have more free time on?
qs.a6: I relax by doing my skincare, watching videos or walking around West Lake. I have more free time on Sunday, because Saturday I often do housework or meet friends.
qs.a7: I unwind by pampering myself with some skincare, watching videos or strolling around West Lake. Sunday gives me more free time, as Saturdays are usually taken up by chores and friends.

qs.q: Are you planning to do anything special next weekend? / Is there an activity you would like to try?
qs.a6: Not really, I'll probably stay home and rest. But I would like to try cycling or swimming because I need more exercise.
qs.a7: Nothing special; I'll probably catch up on sleep. I'd like to try swimming or cycling, though, as I need to get more exercise.

qs.q: Do you prefer to do free-time activities alone or with others? / What free-time activities are popular in your country?
qs.a6: I like both. Alone I can relax, with others it's more fun. In Vietnam, people like having coffee, singing karaoke, playing football and eating out.
qs.a7: A bit of both: solo time to recharge, company for fun. In Vietnam, popular pastimes include café-hopping, karaoke, football and eating out.

qs.q: How do your surrounding friends relax?
qs.a6: They play games, go for coffee, play football or just sleep at home.
qs.a7: Some play games, some meet for coffee or football, and some simply sleep in.

qs.q: Do you often have free time?
qs.a6: Not much on weekdays. I mostly have free time in the evening and at weekends.
qs.a7: Not much on weekdays; mostly evenings and weekends.

qs.q: Would you like to have more free time in the future?
qs.a6: Yes, I'd like to have more time for my family, exercise and travel.
qs.a7: Definitely, for family, exercise and travelling.

qs.q: Who do you usually spend your spare time with?
qs.a6: With my friends, my brother, and sometimes alone.
qs.a7: Friends and my brother, and sometimes just by myself.

qs.q: Favourite free-time activity as a child?
qs.a6: Playing football and flying kites with the neighbours' children.
qs.a7: Playing football and flying kites with the kids in my neighbourhood.

topics.title: Music

qs.q: What music do you like? / What kinds of music do you listen to?
qs.a6: I like pop and ballads, and sometimes K-pop. These songs are easy to listen to and help me relax.
qs.a7: Mostly pop and ballads, with a bit of K-pop. They're easy listening and help me wind down.

qs.q: Do you prefer sad or happy music? / Does happy music make you feel more excited?
qs.a6: I prefer slow, sad songs when I'm tired, but happy music makes me more energetic, for example when I clean my room.
qs.a7: Slow, melancholic songs when I'm tired, but upbeat music definitely lifts my mood and gives me energy, especially when I'm doing chores.

qs.q: What music do your friends like? Do you enjoy the same type?
qs.a6: My friends like pop and rap. We have a few songs in common, but I don't enjoy rap very much.
qs.a7: Pop and rap, mostly. We overlap on a few songs, but rap isn't really my cup of tea.

qs.q: What's the most popular type of music where you live? / Which singer would you like to see in person?
qs.a6: Pop and V-pop are the most popular. I would like to see a famous Vietnamese singer, because I love his songs and I want to feel the atmosphere of a live concert.
qs.a7: Pop and V-pop. I'd love to see a favourite Vietnamese singer live, to experience the electric atmosphere of a concert.

qs.q: Is it easy to learn music? / Do you learn music at school?
qs.a6: I think it isn't easy, because you need to practise a lot. At school, we had simple music lessons, but they weren't very serious.
qs.a7: Not really; it takes plenty of practice. We had basic music lessons at school, but nothing in depth.

qs.q: Do you often listen to one type of music?
qs.a6: Mostly pop and ballads, but sometimes I listen to others to change my mood.
qs.a7: Mostly pop and ballads, though I occasionally switch genres to change my mood.

topics.title: Tidy

qs.q: Are you a tidy person? / Do you like to keep things tidy?
qs.a6: Yes, I am. I like my room to be clean and neat, so I feel comfortable and can find things easily.
qs.a7: Yes, I'd say so. I like my room neat and tidy, as it keeps my mind clear and I can find things quickly.

qs.q: How do you usually keep your place tidy?
qs.a6: I put things back after using them, and I clean my room on weekends. I also try to throw away things that I don't need.
qs.a7: I put things back where they belong, do a proper clean at the weekend and regularly declutter anything I don't need.

qs.q: Are you tidier at work or at home?
qs.a6: I'm tidier at home. At work, I have many papers and cables on my desk, but I try to arrange them before I go home.
qs.a7: At home. My work desk gets cluttered with notes and cables, but I tidy it up before leaving.

qs.q: Were you a tidy person when you were a child?
qs.a6: No, I wasn't. My mother often asked me to clean my room. I changed when I started working.
qs.a7: Not at all. My mother was constantly nagging me to clean my room. I only changed once I started working.

qs.q: What do you think of people who are untidy / overly tidy? / Should people be tidy all the time?
qs.a6: I don't mind untidy people if they are good people. But overly tidy people can be stressful for others. I think it's difficult to be tidy all the time.
qs.a7: I'm fairly easy-going about untidiness, but overly tidy people can be stressful to live with. Staying tidy all the time is unrealistic; a bit of balance is healthier.

topics.title: Website

qs.q: What kinds of websites do you often visit? / What is your favourite website?
qs.a6: I often visit news websites, YouTube and shopping websites. My favourite is YouTube, because I can learn and relax there.
qs.a7: News sites, YouTube and online shopping platforms. YouTube is my favourite, as I can both learn and unwind there.

qs.q: What kinds of websites are popular in your country? / Are there any changes to the websites you often visit?
qs.a6: Social media, online shopping and news websites are popular. The websites I use are changing; they have more videos and the design is easier to use.
qs.a7: Social media, e-commerce and news sites. The ones I use have evolved a lot, with more video content and more user-friendly designs.

qs.q: Do you prefer to search for information through websites or books?
qs.a6: I prefer websites because they are fast and free. But for studying English, I think books are more reliable.
qs.a7: Websites, for speed and convenience, although for serious study, such as English, I find books more reliable.

qs.q: Do you want to create your own website in the future?
qs.a6: Maybe. I work in IT, so I think it's not too hard. I'd like to make a website to share my English learning notes.
qs.a7: Possibly. Given my IT background, it wouldn't be too difficult, and I'd like to build one to share my English study notes.

qs.q: Do you usually use websites?
qs.a6: Yes, every day, for work, news and learning English.
qs.a7: Yes, daily, for work, news and English study.

topics.title: Watches

qs.q: Do you wear a watch? / Do you often check the time?
qs.a6: No, I don't wear a watch now. I check the time on my phone. But I had a watch when I was a student.
qs.a7: Not these days. I just glance at my phone, though I used to wear a watch back in my student days.

qs.q: Have you ever received a watch as a gift? / Would you give a watch as a gift?
qs.a6: Yes, my parents gave me a watch on my birthday. I think a watch is a good gift because it is useful and people can use it for a long time.
qs.a7: Yes, my parents gave me one for my birthday. A watch makes a thoughtful gift, as it's practical and long-lasting.

qs.q: Do you think smartwatches are better than normal watches?
qs.a6: For me, yes. Smartwatches can count steps, check messages and track sleep. But normal watches look more classic and the battery lasts longer.
qs.a7: In terms of features, yes: they track steps and sleep and show notifications. Traditional watches, however, look more classic and have better battery life.

qs.q: Are watches popular in your country? / Do you think watches are important to people?
qs.a6: Yes, many people wear watches, especially men, as an accessory. I think they are not very important now, because phones show the time.
qs.a7: They're fairly popular, especially as fashion accessories, though they've become less essential now that phones tell the time.

qs.q: Did you wear a watch as a child?
qs.a6: Yes, a cartoon watch. My parents bought it so I wouldn't be late for school.
qs.a7: Yes, a cartoon watch my parents bought so I'd be on time for school.

qs.q: Why do people enjoy expensive watches?
qs.a6: They show status and success, and good watches have beautiful design and last long. Some people collect them as an investment.
qs.a7: They signal status and success, boast fine craftsmanship and longevity, and some treat them as investments.

qs.q: Is a watch important for you?
qs.a6: Not very, because I use my phone. But a watch helps me be on time.
qs.a7: Not really, as my phone does the job, though a watch does help with punctuality.

qs.q: What kind of watch do you have?
qs.a6: A simple black watch with a leather strap, but I rarely wear it.
qs.a7: A simple black watch with a leather strap, which I rarely wear.

topics.title: Shopping

qs.q: Do you like shopping? / How often do you go shopping?
qs.a6: Yes, I like it, especially buying skincare products and clothes. I go shopping about twice a month.
qs.a7: Yes, particularly for skincare and clothes. I go roughly twice a month.

qs.q: Do you prefer shopping online or in stores?
qs.a6: I prefer online shopping because it's convenient and often cheaper. But for clothes, I like to go to the store to try them on.
qs.a7: Online, for the convenience and better prices, although I like trying clothes on in store.

qs.q: Who do you usually go shopping with?
qs.a6: I usually go with my friends or my brother. They give me opinions about what I buy.
qs.a7: Usually friends or my brother, as it's useful to get a second opinion.

qs.q: What do you usually buy? / Do you plan before shopping?
qs.a6: I usually buy clothes, skincare and some food. Yes, I make a short list on my phone, so I don't spend too much.
qs.a7: Clothes, skincare and groceries mostly. I jot down a short list on my phone to avoid overspending.

qs.q: Have you ever bought something you regret? / Have shopping habits changed in your country?
qs.a6: Yes, I once bought an expensive shirt, but I never wore it. In my country, more people now shop online and pay by phone.
qs.a7: Yes, an expensive shirt I never wore. Shopping habits have shifted too, as more people now buy online and pay by phone.

qs.q: Favourite shop? Supermarket or store?
qs.a6: My favourite is a skincare shop near my office. I prefer supermarkets for food because I can find everything.
qs.a7: A skincare shop near my office; for groceries, I prefer supermarkets as everything is in one place.

qs.q: Shops near your house? What kinds?
qs.a6: Yes, there are a small supermarket, grocery shops, a pharmacy and some coffee shops.
qs.a7: Yes: a small supermarket, grocery stores, a pharmacy and a few cafés.

qs.q: Shopping centres?
qs.a6: Yes, sometimes at weekends, because they have shops, food and cinemas.
qs.a7: Sometimes at weekends, for the mix of shops, food and cinemas.

qs.q: Traditional markets?
qs.a6: Yes, they have fresh food and cheaper prices, and I can bargain. But they are hot and crowded.
qs.a7: Yes, for fresh produce and bargain prices, although they're hot and crowded.

qs.q: How much do you spend on clothes?
qs.a6: About one million dong a month.
qs.a7: Roughly a million dong a month.

qs.q: Formal event like a wedding?
qs.a6: A white shirt, dark trousers and leather shoes, or a suit.
qs.a7: A white shirt, dark trousers and leather shoes, or a suit.

qs.q: Compare prices?
qs.a6: Yes, I always compare on apps before buying.
qs.a7: Always, using apps before I buy.

qs.q: Difficult to make choices?
qs.a6: Sometimes, when there are too many choices. I read reviews.
qs.a7: Occasionally, when there's too much choice, so I read reviews.

topics.title: Cars

qs.q: Do you like cars? / Do you have a car?
qs.a6: Yes, I think cars are useful and comfortable. I don't have a car now, because I take the bus and it's cheaper.
qs.a7: I like them. They're comfortable and practical. I don't own one, though, since the bus is much cheaper for my commute.

qs.q: Do you prefer to drive or be a passenger?
qs.a6: I prefer to be a passenger, because I can rest or listen to music. Driving in Hanoi is very stressful.
qs.a7: Passenger, definitely. I can relax or listen to music, whereas driving in Hanoi's traffic is exhausting.

qs.q: Do you want to buy a car in the future? / What kind of car do you like?
qs.a6: Yes, maybe in five years, when I have enough money. I like a small, economical car which is easy to park.
qs.a7: Possibly in five years, once I can afford it. I'd go for a compact, fuel-efficient car that's easy to park.

qs.q: Are cars popular in your country? / Do you think there are too many cars?
qs.a6: More and more people buy cars now, so there are too many in big cities. It causes traffic jams and pollution.
qs.a7: Increasingly so. In big cities there are too many, which leads to congestion and air pollution.

qs.q: Did you enjoy travelling by car as a kid?
qs.a6: Yes, but I often felt dizzy on long trips.
qs.a7: Yes, although I got carsick on long trips.

qs.q: What do you do in a traffic jam?
qs.a6: On the bus, I listen to music or study English.
qs.a7: On the bus, I listen to music or practise English.

qs.q: Lots of cars in your city?
qs.a6: Yes, too many, so traffic jams happen every day.
qs.a7: Yes, far too many, which causes daily traffic jams.

qs.q: Want an expensive car?
qs.a6: No. I want a normal reliable car, because expensive cars cost too much to maintain.
qs.a7: No, a reliable ordinary car will do; expensive ones cost too much to maintain.

topics.title: Feeling bored

qs.q: What do you do when you feel bored? / Do you often feel bored?
qs.a6: Not often. When I'm bored, I listen to music, watch short videos or chat with my friends.
qs.a7: Not very often. When I am, I put on music, scroll through short videos or message a friend.

qs.q: Are there any places where you feel bored? / Do you feel bored at work?
qs.a6: Yes, in long meetings or in a traffic jam. At work, sometimes I do repeated tasks, like running the same test cases, and it feels boring.
qs.a7: Yes, long meetings and traffic jams. At work, repetitive tasks such as running the same test cases over and over can get monotonous.

qs.q: Do you think children feel bored more easily than adults?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. Children have lots of energy and a short attention span, so they need games or activities all the time.
qs.a7: I think so. Kids have boundless energy and short attention spans, so they constantly need stimulation.

qs.q: What can people do to avoid being bored?
qs.a6: They can find a hobby, exercise or learn something new. Spending time with friends also helps.
qs.a7: Take up a hobby, exercise, learn something new or simply spend time with friends.

qs.q: School boring as a child?
qs.a6: Sometimes, in long theory lessons like history.
qs.a7: At times, during long theoretical lessons such as history.

qs.q: What do you find most boring now?
qs.a6: Repeating the same tasks at work, and long meetings.
qs.a7: Repetitive tasks at work and lengthy meetings.

topics.title: Telling jokes

qs.q: Do you like telling jokes? / Do you often tell jokes?
qs.a6: Not very often. I'm a quiet person, but I sometimes tell jokes to my close friends and my colleagues.
qs.a7: Not that often. I'm rather reserved, but I do crack jokes with close friends and colleagues.

qs.q: Who tells the best jokes among your friends/family?
qs.a6: My friend Hung. He is very funny and he can make everyone laugh, even when he tells a simple story.
qs.a7: My friend Hung. He has a real knack for making everybody laugh, even with a simple story.

qs.q: Do you like jokes on the internet / from TV? / What makes you laugh?
qs.a6: Yes, I like funny videos and memes. They are short and easy to understand, and they make me relax after work.
qs.a7: Yes, funny videos and memes in particular. They're short, relatable and a great way to unwind after work.

qs.q: Is it important to have a sense of humour? / Are there jokes you should not tell?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. Humour helps us to reduce stress and make friends. But we should not tell jokes about someone's appearance or family, because they can be hurt.
qs.a7: Yes, humour relieves stress and helps build friendships. However, jokes about someone's appearance or family are best avoided, as they can hurt people's feelings.

qs.q: Common comedy shows in your country?
qs.a6: There are TV comedy shows at Tet, stand-up comedy and funny online skits.
qs.a7: Tet comedy specials on TV, stand-up shows and popular online skits.

qs.q: Do you like being joked about?
qs.a6: It's OK if it's light and from close friends. I don't like jokes about my family.
qs.a7: Fine if it's light-hearted and from close friends, but not about my family.

topics.title: Reading carefully

qs.q: Do you read things carefully? / Do you read slowly or quickly?
qs.a6: Yes, I do, especially at work. I read requirements carefully to find mistakes. But for entertainment, I read fast.
qs.a7: Yes, especially at work, where I scrutinise requirements to spot errors. For leisure reading, I tend to skim.

qs.q: What things do you need to read carefully? / Did you read carefully when you were young?
qs.a6: I need to read contracts, emails and instructions carefully. When I was young, I wasn't careful, so I made small mistakes in exams.
qs.a7: Contracts, important emails and instructions. As a child I was careless, which cost me marks in exams.

qs.q: Do you think reading carefully is important? / How can people read more carefully?
qs.a6: Yes, it's very important because it helps us avoid mistakes. People can read slowly, underline key points and not use their phones at the same time.
qs.a7: Absolutely, as it prevents costly mistakes. Reading slowly, underlining key points and putting the phone away all help.

qs.q: Do you prefer reading on paper or on screen?
qs.a6: I prefer paper when I need to focus, but I read on my phone more because it's convenient, especially on the bus.
qs.a7: Paper for focus, but screens are more convenient, especially on the bus.

qs.q: Why don't some people read messages carefully?
qs.a6: They are busy or reading on the phone while doing other things, so they only read quickly. Messages are also short and look unimportant.
qs.a7: They're busy or multitasking, and short messages seem unimportant.

topics.note: Thông tin giả định theo hồ sơ: IT Tester ở Hà Nội, sống ngoại thành. Bạn sửa chi tiết khi nói rồi gửi mình chấm.

topics.title: Parks and gardens

qs.q: Do you often go to parks? / Are there parks near your home?
qs.a6: Sometimes, on weekends. There is a small park near my house where people walk and do exercise in the morning.
qs.a7: Occasionally at weekends. There's a small park near my home where people walk and exercise in the mornings.

qs.q: What do people usually do in parks?
qs.a6: They walk, jog, do exercise, play with children or sit and talk. Old people often play chess.
qs.a7: Walk, jog, exercise, play with their kids or simply chat. The elderly often play chess.

qs.q: Do you prefer parks or gardens? / Do you want to have a garden?
qs.a6: I prefer parks because they are bigger and have more activities. A garden at home would be nice, but my house is small.
qs.a7: Parks, as they're larger with more to do. A garden would be lovely, but my house doesn't have space.

qs.q: Are parks important for a city? / Should the government build more parks?
qs.a6: Yes, because parks give fresh air and a place to relax. In Hanoi, the air is polluted, so I think we need more parks.
qs.a7: Yes, they provide fresh air and a place to unwind. With Hanoi's air pollution, more parks would be welcome.

qs.q: Last time you went to a park?
qs.a6: Two weeks ago, I walked around a park with my friend on Sunday.
qs.a7: A fortnight ago, I strolled around a park with a friend on a Sunday.

qs.q: Do people in your country go to parks often?
qs.a6: Yes, many people exercise in parks in the morning and evening.
qs.a7: Yes, many exercise there in the early morning and evening.

qs.q: Childhood parks and the one near home?
qs.a6: There was a small playground near my home. I played on the swings and flew kites there.
qs.a7: A small playground near home, where I played on swings and flew kites.

qs.q: Enjoy now?
qs.a6: Yes, they help me relax after work.
qs.a7: Yes, they help me unwind after work.

qs.q: Famous park you want to visit?
qs.a6: Central Park in New York, because I have seen it in many films.
qs.a7: Central Park in New York, which I've seen in countless films.

topics.note: Thông tin giả định theo hồ sơ: IT Tester ở Hà Nội, sống ngoại thành. Bạn sửa chi tiết khi nói rồi gửi mình chấm.

topics.title: Headphones

qs.q: Do you use headphones? / How often do you use them?
qs.a6: Yes, almost every day. I use them on the bus to listen to music or to study English.
qs.a7: Almost every day, mainly on the bus, for music or English listening practice.

qs.q: What kind of headphones do you like? / Have you ever bought headphones?
qs.a6: I like wireless earphones because they are light and have no cable. I bought mine online last year.
qs.a7: Wireless earbuds, as they're lightweight and tangle-free. I bought mine online last year.

qs.q: Do you think it's OK to use headphones in public places?
qs.a6: Yes, if the volume is low. It's better than playing music loudly. But on the street it's dangerous, because we can't hear cars.
qs.a7: Yes, provided the volume is low, which is better than blasting music aloud. On the road, though, it can be dangerous as you can't hear traffic.

qs.q: Are headphones popular among young people? / Do headphones affect our health?
qs.a6: Yes, very popular. But using loud headphones for a long time can damage our ears.
qs.a7: Very popular. However, prolonged use at high volume can damage hearing.

qs.q: Are headphones useful?
qs.a6: Yes, for music, calls and studying. They block noise.
qs.a7: Yes, for music, calls and studying, and they cut out noise.

qs.q: When should people not wear them?
qs.a6: When crossing the road or riding a motorbike, and in meetings. They can't hear danger.
qs.a7: While crossing roads, riding a motorbike or in meetings, since they can't hear danger.

topics.title: Travelling

qs.q: Do you like travelling? / How often do you travel?
qs.a6: Yes, I love it. I travel two or three times a year, usually on public holidays, because I'm busy with work.
qs.a7: Yes, I love it. I manage two or three trips a year, mostly over public holidays, given my work schedule.

qs.q: Do you prefer to travel alone or with others? / Who do you usually travel with?
qs.a6: I prefer travelling with friends or family. It's safer and more fun, and we can share the cost.
qs.a7: With friends or family. It's safer, more enjoyable and we can split the costs.

qs.q: What was your most memorable trip?
qs.a6: I went to Da Nang with my friends two years ago. We swam in the sea, ate seafood and took a lot of photos. It was really relaxing.
qs.a7: A trip to Da Nang with friends two years ago. We swam, feasted on seafood and took countless photos; it was the perfect break.

qs.q: Is there a place you want to visit in the future? / What do you usually do when you travel?
qs.a6: I want to visit Japan because the scenery is beautiful and the culture is interesting. When I travel, I try local food and take photos.
qs.a7: Japan, for its stunning scenery and fascinating culture. When I travel, I sample local dishes and take plenty of photos.

qs.q: Do you look at the view when travelling?
qs.a6: Yes, I always look out of the window of the bus or the train. It's relaxing.
qs.a7: Always. Watching the scenery from a window is relaxing.

qs.q: Travelled far as a child?
qs.a6: Not really. I went to my grandmother's village by bus, about 150 km, once a year.
qs.a7: Not really; just my annual bus trip to my grandmother's village, about 150 km away.

qs.q: Mountain or ocean views?
qs.a6: Ocean views. The sea makes me feel free.
qs.a7: Ocean views, as the sea gives me a sense of freedom.

qs.q: Photo of a beautiful view?
qs.a6: Yes, always, with my phone.
qs.a7: Yes, I always snap a quick photo.

qs.q: Hang a picture at home?
qs.a6: Yes, a sea picture would make my room feel calm.
qs.a7: Yes, a seascape would give my room a calming feel.

topics.title: Daily routine

qs.q: What is your daily routine? / What do you usually do on a typical day?
qs.a6: I get up at 6:30, do my skincare and have breakfast. Then I take the bus to work. I work from 8:30 to 5:30, and in the evening I study English and relax.
qs.a7: I'm up by 6:30, do my skincare, grab breakfast and catch the bus to work. I'm in the office from 8:30 to 5:30, then I spend my evenings on English and unwinding.

qs.q: Which part of the day do you like best? / Do you like to have the same routine every day?
qs.a6: I like the evening best, because I'm free and can relax. I like a regular routine, because it makes me feel organised, but sometimes I want a change.
qs.a7: The evening, when I'm free to relax. I like a steady routine as it keeps me organised, though I occasionally crave a change.

qs.q: Do you want to change your daily routine? / Is your routine different on weekends?
qs.a6: Yes, I want to get up earlier to exercise. On weekends I get up later and have no fixed schedule.
qs.a7: Yes, I'd like to wake up earlier to fit in some exercise. At weekends, I sleep in and have no fixed schedule.

qs.q: Is it important to have a daily routine?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. A good routine helps us use our time well and keeps us healthy.
qs.a7: Yes, a good routine helps us manage our time and stay healthy.

qs.q: Go to bed late or early? Stay up late?
qs.a6: Quite late, around 11:30, because I study English and use my phone. I stay up late sometimes on weekends.
qs.a7: Fairly late, around 11:30, studying English and scrolling my phone, and later at weekends.

qs.q: Daily study routine and how you organise study time?
qs.a6: I study English for about one hour in the evening and fifteen minutes in the morning. I use a plan on Notion and write what to do for each day.
qs.a7: About an hour in the evening and fifteen minutes in the morning, with a Notion plan listing each day's tasks.

qs.q: Changed routine or plans?
qs.a6: Yes, after I started working, I got up earlier. I change plans when I have urgent work.
qs.a7: Yes, I started waking up earlier after I began work, and I adjust plans when urgent tasks come up.

topics.title: Stages in life

qs.q: Which stage of life do you think is the happiest? / Which stage are you in now?
qs.a6: I think childhood is the happiest, because you have no worries. Now I'm in the early stage of my career, and I'm busy but I'm learning a lot.
qs.a7: Childhood, as it's free of worries. I'm currently at the start of my career, which is busy but full of learning.

qs.q: What was the best stage of your life so far?
qs.a6: University was the best. I had many friends and I could try new things without too much pressure.
qs.a7: My university years. I made great friends and could try new things without much pressure.

qs.q: What do you look forward to in the next stage of your life?
qs.a6: I look forward to a better job, a stable income and maybe a family of my own.
qs.a7: A better position, a steady income and, eventually, a family of my own.

qs.q: What are the differences between young people and old people?
qs.a6: Young people are more energetic and like new things. Old people have more experience and prefer a quiet, stable life.
qs.a7: Young people are energetic and open to novelty, while older people bring experience and favour a calm, stable life.

qs.q: How do people remember each stage of their lives?
qs.a6: Through photos, videos, diaries and souvenirs. Family stories are also important.
qs.a7: Through photos, videos, diaries and souvenirs, as well as family stories.

qs.q: Enjoy / satisfied with your age now?
qs.a6: Yes, mostly. I'm independent and have energy, but I have more pressure.
qs.a7: Mostly, yes. I'm independent and energetic, though under more pressure.

qs.q: Childhood with friends / what you enjoyed most?
qs.a6: We played football and kites. I enjoyed the freedom and having no worries.
qs.a7: We played football and flew kites. What I enjoyed most was the freedom and the lack of worries.

qs.q: Plans for the next five years? What is the most important now?
qs.a6: I plan to achieve IELTS 6.5 and become a senior tester. The most important thing now is to improve my skills.
qs.a7: To reach IELTS 6.5 and become a senior tester; at the moment, building my skills is the priority.

qs.q: Most important thing you've done so far?
qs.a6: Graduating from university and getting a stable job.
qs.a7: Graduating and securing a stable job.

topics.title: Views

qs.q: Do you like views / beautiful scenery? / What views do you like?
qs.a6: Yes, I love sea views and mountain views. They make me feel peaceful and happy.
qs.a7: Yes, especially sea and mountain views, which instantly calm me.

qs.q: Is there a nice view near your home or workplace?
qs.a6: Near my home, there is a rice field and a small river, and it's beautiful at sunset. At work, the view is just buildings.
qs.a7: Near my home there are rice fields and a small river that look lovely at sunset. My office view, however, is just buildings.

qs.q: Do you take photos of beautiful views? / Do you want to live in a place with a nice view?
qs.a6: Yes, I take photos with my phone and share them with friends. I'd like to live in a place with a nice view, but houses there are expensive.
qs.a7: Yes, I snap photos on my phone and share them with friends. I'd love a home with a good view, although such places are pricey.

qs.q: Are views important for tourism?
qs.a6: Yes, very important. Many tourists come to Vietnam to see Ha Long Bay and Sa Pa. Beautiful views create jobs for local people.
qs.a7: Absolutely. Many visitors come to see Ha Long Bay and Sa Pa, and stunning scenery creates jobs for locals.

qs.q: Urban or rural views?
qs.a6: Rural views, because they are green and quiet. City views are nice at night.
qs.a7: Rural views, for their greenery and calm, though city skylines are lovely at night.

qs.q: Views in your country or abroad?
qs.a6: Both, but views abroad are new to me. I'd like to see views of Japan.
qs.a7: Both, though foreign views feel fresh; I'd love to see Japan's.

topics.title: Hobbies

qs.q: What are your hobbies? / Do you have any hobbies?
qs.a6: I like listening to music, watching films and taking care of my skin. I also like walking in the evening.
qs.a7: Listening to music, watching films, skincare and evening walks are my main pastimes.

qs.q: Did you have a different hobby when you were a child?
qs.a6: Yes, I liked playing football with my neighbours and playing computer games.
qs.a7: Yes, I used to kick a ball around with the neighbourhood kids and play computer games.

qs.q: Do you spend a lot of money on your hobbies?
qs.a6: A little. I spend some money on skincare products and cinema tickets, but my hobbies are not expensive.
qs.a7: Not a lot. Some goes on skincare and cinema tickets, but my hobbies are fairly inexpensive.

qs.q: Is it important to have a hobby? / Would you like to try a new hobby?
qs.a6: Yes, a hobby helps us relax after work. I'd like to try swimming or photography.
qs.a7: Yes, a hobby is a great way to decompress after work. I'd like to try swimming or photography.

qs.q: Same hobbies as family?
qs.a6: Some. My brother and I both like films, and my mother likes music like me.
qs.a7: Partly. My brother and I both love films, and my mother shares my taste in music.

qs.q: A hobby since childhood?
qs.a6: Yes, listening to music. I have loved it since I was a child.
qs.a7: Yes, listening to music, which I've loved since I was little.

topics.title: Typing

qs.q: Do you type a lot? / Can you type fast?
qs.a6: Yes, a lot. I type reports and test cases every day at work. I can type quite fast and I don't need to look at the keyboard.
qs.a7: Constantly. I write reports and test cases daily, so I'm a fairly fast touch typist.

qs.q: When did you learn to type? / Did you learn typing at school?
qs.a6: I learned at secondary school in IT class. Then I practised more at university.
qs.a7: I picked it up in IT class at secondary school, then honed the skill at university.

qs.q: Do you prefer typing or handwriting?
qs.a6: I prefer typing because it's faster and easier to correct. But I think handwriting is better for remembering things.
qs.a7: Typing, for speed and easy editing, although handwriting helps me remember things better.

qs.q: Will people stop handwriting in the future?
qs.a6: Maybe not completely. Children still need to learn handwriting, but adults will write by hand less and less.
qs.a7: Probably not entirely. Children will still learn it, but adults will increasingly rely on keyboards and voice input.

qs.q: Desktop or laptop keyboard? How often?
qs.a6: A laptop at work, for most of the day, every day.
qs.a7: A laptop, for most of the working day.

qs.q: Improve typing?
qs.a6: I practise with online typing tests and use shortcuts. Yes, I want to type faster.
qs.a7: With online typing tests and keyboard shortcuts; I'd like to get even faster.

qs.q: Easier: typing or handwriting?
qs.a6: Typing is easier and faster. Handwriting is tiring.
qs.a7: Typing is quicker and less tiring.

topics.title: Scenery

qs.q: Do you like beautiful scenery? / What kind of scenery do you like?
qs.a6: Yes, I like green mountains, rivers and beaches. They help me relax after stressful days.
qs.a7: Yes, particularly green mountains, rivers and beaches, which help me recover from stressful days.

qs.q: What's the most beautiful scenery in your country?
qs.a6: I think Ha Long Bay and Ninh Binh are very beautiful. There are green mountains and calm water.
qs.a7: Ha Long Bay and Ninh Binh, with their limestone mountains and tranquil water, are stunning.

qs.q: Do you like to take photos of scenery? / Do you prefer scenery in the countryside or in the city?
qs.a6: Yes, I take many photos. I prefer the countryside because the air is fresh and the space is open.
qs.a7: Yes, plenty. I prefer the countryside for its fresh air and wide-open spaces.

qs.q: Does beautiful scenery make people happier?
qs.a6: I think so. When we look at nature, we feel less stressed and more positive.
qs.a7: I believe so. Being surrounded by nature eases stress and lifts our mood.

qs.q: Where can you enjoy beautiful views near you?
qs.a6: Rice fields and the river near my house, and West Lake in the city.
qs.a7: The rice fields and river by my house, and West Lake in the city.

qs.q: Best view / most beautiful sights?
qs.a6: The sea at sunrise in Da Nang, and Ha Long Bay.
qs.a7: The sunrise over the sea in Da Nang, and Ha Long Bay.

qs.q: Do you book rooms with good views?
qs.a6: Yes, if the price is OK. A sea view makes the trip special.
qs.a7: Yes, if the price is reasonable, since a sea view makes a trip special.

qs.q: Look out the window on the bus or car?
qs.a6: Yes, I always do. It makes the journey less boring.
qs.a7: Always; it makes journeys less dull.

qs.q: Mountains or sea?
qs.a6: The sea, because it's open and relaxing.
qs.a7: The sea, for its openness and calm.

topics.title: Buildings

qs.q: Do you like the buildings in your city? / What types of buildings are there in your area?
qs.a6: Hanoi has old French-style buildings and modern high-rise buildings. I like the old ones because they are beautiful and have history. In my area, most are small houses.
qs.a7: Hanoi blends old French colonial buildings with modern skyscrapers. I prefer the old ones for their charm and history. My area mostly has small family houses.

qs.q: Is there any interesting building you like? / What is your favourite building?
qs.a6: I like Hanoi Opera House. It has a classic design and looks beautiful at night.
qs.a7: The Hanoi Opera House, with its classic architecture, looks magnificent at night.

qs.q: Do you prefer old buildings or modern ones?
qs.a6: I like both, but I prefer old buildings. They have a special atmosphere. Modern buildings are more useful, though.
qs.a7: Old ones, for their atmosphere, though modern buildings are undoubtedly more functional.

qs.q: Should old buildings be preserved?
qs.a6: Yes, because they are part of our culture and history. If we destroy them, we can't get them back.
qs.a7: Yes, they're part of our heritage, and once demolished, they're gone forever.

qs.q: Tall buildings near home? Tallest building in your city?
qs.a6: Not near my home, because it's the suburbs. The tallest building in Hanoi is Landmark 72, I think.
qs.a7: Not near my home in the suburbs. The tallest in Hanoi is, I believe, Landmark 72.

qs.q: Take photos of buildings?
qs.a6: Sometimes, if they're old or very beautiful.
qs.a7: Occasionally, when they're old or especially beautiful.

qs.q: Building you'd like to visit?
qs.a6: The Imperial City in Hue, because I like history.
qs.a7: The Imperial City in Hue, given my interest in history.

qs.q: What building would you like to live in?
qs.a6: A modern apartment near the city centre, or a house with a small garden.
qs.a7: A modern central apartment, or a house with a small garden.

topics.title: Childhood activities

qs.q: What did you like to do when you were a child? / What were your favourite activities?
qs.a6: I liked playing outside with my neighbours, such as football, hide-and-seek and flying kites. I also liked watching cartoons.
qs.a7: I loved playing outdoors with the neighbourhood kids: football, hide-and-seek and flying kites. I was also glued to cartoons.

qs.q: Do you still do these activities now?
qs.a6: Not really. I'm too busy, and my friends also live far away. Sometimes I play football with colleagues, but not often.
qs.a7: Rarely. Work keeps me busy and my old friends live far away, though I occasionally play football with colleagues.

qs.q: Did you play with your friends or alone? / Did your parents join you?
qs.a6: Mostly with friends. My father sometimes taught me how to ride a bike, and my mother cooked for us after we played.
qs.a7: Mostly with friends. My father occasionally joined in, teaching me to ride a bike, while my mother had food waiting afterwards.

qs.q: Do you think children today play differently? / Is it good for children to play outdoors?
qs.a6: Yes, now children play with phones and tablets more. I think outdoor play is better because it's healthy and helps them make friends.
qs.a7: Yes, they're far more screen-focused. Outdoor play is healthier and helps children develop social skills.

qs.q: Alone or with a group?
qs.a6: With a group, because games like football need many people. Sometimes I read comics alone.
qs.a7: In a group, as games like football need teammates, though I read comics alone occasionally.

qs.q: Did you enjoy your childhood?
qs.a6: Yes, very much. It was simple, but happy.
qs.a7: Very much. It was simple but happy.

topics.title: Morning time

qs.q: Do you like mornings? / Are you a morning person?
qs.a6: Not really. I'm not a morning person, but I like quiet mornings on weekends. I need coffee to wake up.
qs.a7: Not really. I'm no early bird, but I do enjoy quiet weekend mornings, and I need a coffee to get going.

qs.q: What do you usually do in the morning?
qs.a6: I wash my face, do my skincare, eat breakfast and take the bus to work. I usually listen to music on the bus.
qs.a7: I wash up, do my skincare, have breakfast and take the bus to work, listening to music on the way.

qs.q: What time do you usually get up? / Do you get up earlier on weekdays?
qs.a6: At 6:30 on weekdays and about 8:00 on weekends. I have to leave home early, because my house is far from the office.
qs.a7: Around 6:30 on weekdays and 8:00 at weekends. I have to leave early as my home is far from the office.

qs.q: Is the morning a good time for studying or working?
qs.a6: Yes, I think so. My head is clear and there are fewer distractions. I try to learn English for fifteen minutes before going to work.
qs.a7: Yes, the mind is fresh and there are fewer distractions. I try to squeeze in fifteen minutes of English before work.

qs.q: Same morning routine on weekdays and weekends?
qs.a6: Weekdays are busy and fixed. Weekends are slower: I sleep late and have breakfast at home.
qs.a7: Weekdays are rushed and fixed; at weekends I sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast.

qs.q: Eat breakfast at home?
qs.a6: Sometimes. On workdays, I buy banh mi or sticky rice near the bus stop.
qs.a7: Sometimes; on workdays I grab a banh mi or sticky rice near the bus stop.

qs.q: Morning now vs in the past / when little?
qs.a6: When I was little, I got up at 6:00 to go to school, and my mother cooked breakfast. Now I do everything by myself.
qs.a7: As a child I got up at 6 for school with breakfast cooked by my mother; now I manage everything myself.

qs.q: Favourite morning of the week?
qs.a6: Sunday, because I can sleep late and have a slow coffee.
qs.a7: Sunday, when I can sleep in and enjoy a slow coffee.

topics.title: Gift

qs.q: Do you like giving gifts? / Do you often give gifts?
qs.a6: Yes, I do. I give gifts on birthdays and holidays, like Tet. I like to see people happy when they get my gift.
qs.a7: Yes, on birthdays and holidays such as Tet. I love seeing the joy on people's faces when they open a present.

qs.q: What was the last gift you gave? / What gift would you give to a friend?
qs.a6: I gave my mother a scarf on her birthday. For a friend, I would choose a book or skincare products, which are useful.
qs.a7: A scarf for my mother's birthday. For a friend, I'd pick a book or skincare set, something practical.

qs.q: Do you prefer to receive gifts or give gifts?
qs.a6: I prefer giving gifts, because I feel happy when I make others happy. But I also like to receive gifts, of course.
qs.a7: Giving, as making others happy makes me happy, though receiving is nice too, of course.

qs.q: Is it important to give gifts? / Do you like handmade gifts?
qs.a6: Yes, because gifts show our care. Handmade gifts are special because they take time and effort.
qs.a7: Yes, gifts show we care. Handmade ones are especially meaningful, as they take time and effort.

qs.q: Handmade gifts?
qs.a6: Yes, I made a card for my mother on Mother's Day. It was simple, but she loved it.
qs.a7: Yes, a card for my mother on Mother's Day; simple, but she loved it.

qs.q: How to choose a gift?
qs.a6: I think about the person's age, hobby and budget.
qs.a7: I consider the person's age, interests and my budget.

qs.q: A special gift experience?
qs.a6: I gave my brother a keyboard for his birthday. He was very surprised.
qs.a7: I surprised my brother with a keyboard for his birthday, and he was thrilled.

qs.q: Are expensive gifts a good way to express feelings?
qs.a6: Not always. A thoughtful gift is more important than the price.
qs.a7: Not necessarily; thoughtfulness matters more than price.

qs.q: Great / best / recent gift?
qs.a6: The best was a wireless headset from my parents. Recently, my friend gave me a skincare set.
qs.a7: The best was a wireless headset from my parents; recently a friend gave me a skincare set.

qs.q: Good at choosing gifts?
qs.a6: Not very. I need to ask friends for ideas.
qs.a7: Not especially; I often ask friends for ideas.

qs.q: Popular gifts in your country?
qs.a6: Flowers, cosmetics, clothes, watches and cash in red envelopes at Tet.
qs.a7: Flowers, cosmetics, clothes, watches and lucky money at Tet.

qs.q: Buying gifts online?
qs.a6: It's convenient and has many choices, but we can't see the real quality.
qs.a7: Convenient with a wide choice, but you can't judge the real quality.

topics.title: Reading

qs.q: Do you like reading? / What do you like to read?
qs.a6: Yes, a little. I like reading news, self-help books and some articles about technology.
qs.a7: Yes, to a degree. I enjoy news, self-help books and articles on technology.

qs.q: How often do you read? / When do you read?
qs.a6: I read for about thirty minutes a day, usually on the bus or before bed.
qs.a7: About thirty minutes a day, typically on the bus or before bed.

qs.q: Did you read much when you were a child?
qs.a6: Yes, I liked comic books and short stories. My parents bought me many books.
qs.a7: Yes, mostly comics and short stories. My parents kept me well supplied with books.

qs.q: Do you prefer paper books or e-books? / Is reading important?
qs.a6: I prefer e-books because they are cheap and I can read them on my phone. Reading is important because it gives us knowledge and helps us relax.
qs.a7: E-books, for their price and portability. Reading is important as it broadens our knowledge and helps us relax.

qs.q: Books or movies? Novel adapted into a film?
qs.a6: Movies, because they are faster. But books give more details. I watched "Harry Potter", and the book was better.
qs.a7: Movies for speed, though books offer more detail; I read "Harry Potter" after watching it and found the book better.

qs.q: Habits changed? More or less now?
qs.a6: I read less now, because I am busy and use my phone.
qs.a7: Less now, as work and my phone take up my time.

qs.q: Careful reading or scanning?
qs.a6: I read carefully at work and scan news or social media.
qs.a7: Careful reading for work; scanning for news and social media.

topics.title: Keys

qs.q: Do you carry many keys? / What keys do you carry every day?
qs.a6: Not many. I carry a house key and an office key card. I keep them in my bag.
qs.a7: Just a few: my house key and an office access card, both of which I keep in my bag.

qs.q: Have you ever lost your keys? / What did you do?
qs.a6: Yes, once I lost my house key. I called my mother and waited outside for an hour. After that, I made a spare key.
qs.a7: Yes, once. I had to call my mother and wait outside for an hour, so I had a spare key cut afterwards.

qs.q: Do you keep a spare key? / Where do you keep your keys at home?
qs.a6: Yes, my family keeps a spare key. At home, I put my keys on a hook near the door, so I don't forget them.
qs.a7: Yes, we keep a spare. At home, I hang my keys on a hook by the door so I never misplace them.

qs.q: Will keys be replaced by other things in the future?
qs.a6: I think so. Many buildings now use fingerprints, cards or phones, because they are safer and more convenient.
qs.a7: Probably. Fingerprint locks, cards and phone apps are already common, being safer and more convenient.

qs.q: Forget keys / lock yourself out?
qs.a6: Once. I locked myself out when my family was out, and I waited an hour.
qs.a7: Once, when my family was out; I waited for an hour.

qs.q: Leave your keys with a neighbour?
qs.a6: It's a good idea if you trust them, in case of an emergency.
qs.a7: A good idea if you trust the neighbour, for emergencies.

topics.title: Day off

qs.q: What do you usually do on your day off? / How do you spend your days off?
qs.a6: I usually sleep late, clean my room and meet my friends. Sometimes I go out for coffee or watch a film.
qs.a7: I generally sleep in, tidy my room and catch up with friends over coffee or a film.

qs.q: Do you prefer to stay at home or go out on your day off?
qs.a6: It depends. If I'm tired, I stay at home and rest. If the weather is nice, I go out.
qs.a7: It depends. If I'm worn out, I stay in; if the weather is nice, I head out.

qs.q: What do you do for relaxation? / Do you do housework on your day off?
qs.a6: I listen to music and do my skincare. I also help my mother with housework, such as cooking and washing clothes.
qs.a7: I listen to music and pamper my skin. I also help my mother with chores like cooking and laundry.

qs.q: Would you like to have more days off? / Do you think people should work fewer days a week?
qs.a6: Yes, it would be nice. I could have more time for my family and for studying. But too many days off may be bad for the company.
qs.a7: Yes, it'd give me more time for family and study, although too many days off could hurt productivity.

qs.q: Last time you had days off?
qs.a6: Last month, I had three days off for a public holiday.
qs.a7: Last month, three days off for a public holiday.

qs.q: With parents or friends?
qs.a6: Both. With my parents for family meals, and with friends for coffee or films.
qs.a7: Both: family meals with my parents, coffee or films with friends.

qs.q: If you had a day off tomorrow?
qs.a6: I'd sleep late, then go to West Lake with a friend and have a nice lunch.
qs.a7: I'd sleep in, then head to West Lake with a friend and enjoy a good lunch.
