topics.title: Working with old people

qs.q: Do you work / have you worked with old people? / Would you like to?
qs.a6: At my company, there are some older colleagues. I worked with them and I learned a lot from their experience. I'd like to work with them again.
qs.a7: Yes, I have older colleagues, and I've benefited a lot from their experience. I'd gladly work with them again.

qs.q: What are the advantages of working with old people?
qs.a6: They have more experience, they are patient and they give good advice. They also stay calm when there are problems.
qs.a7: They bring experience and patience, offer sound advice and stay calm under pressure.

qs.q: Are there any disadvantages? / Is it difficult to work with older people?
qs.a6: Sometimes they are slow to learn new technology, and we may have different ideas. But we can usually talk and find a solution.
qs.a7: Occasionally they're slower to adopt new technology and our views differ, but we can generally talk it through.

qs.q: Do you think older people should work longer / retire later?
qs.a6: If they are healthy and want to work, yes. They can share experience. But some people need to rest after many years of work.
qs.a7: If they're healthy and willing, yes, as they can share valuable experience. Others deserve a rest after decades of work.

qs.q: Happy to work / spend time with older people?
qs.a6: Yes. They are calm and share many stories.
qs.a7: Yes; they're calm and full of stories.

qs.q: Talk to elderly people often?
qs.a6: Yes, with my grandmother and neighbours.
qs.a7: Yes, with my grandmother and elderly neighbours.

qs.q: How do you feel about getting old?
qs.a6: A bit worried about health, but I think it's natural. I want to be healthy and have a happy family.
qs.a7: Slightly concerned about health, but it's natural; I hope to stay healthy with a happy family.

topics.title: Pets

qs.q: Do you have a pet? / Have you ever had a pet?
qs.a6: No, I don't have one now. When I was a child, my family had a dog. He was friendly and I played with him a lot.
qs.a7: Not at the moment. When I was little, we had a friendly dog that I played with all the time.

qs.q: Would you like to have a pet? / What pet would you like?
qs.a6: Yes, I'd like a cat because it's clean and quiet. But I'm busy, so I don't have time to take care of it now.
qs.a7: Yes, a cat, as they're clean and low-maintenance. I just don't have the time right now.

qs.q: Why do people keep pets? / Are pets popular in your country?
qs.a6: They want company and they feel happy with animals. Pets are more and more popular, especially cats and dogs.
qs.a7: For companionship and emotional comfort. Pets, especially cats and dogs, are increasingly popular in Vietnam.

qs.q: Is it good for children to have pets?
qs.a6: Yes, because children learn to be responsible and kind. Pets also make children happier.
qs.a7: Yes, it teaches children responsibility and compassion, and they're happier with a companion.

qs.q: Favourite animal?
qs.a6: Dogs, because they are loyal and friendly.
qs.a7: Dogs, for their loyalty and friendliness.

qs.q: Indoors or outdoors?
qs.a6: Indoors for cats, outdoors for dogs with a yard.
qs.a7: Cats indoors; dogs outdoors if there's a yard.

qs.q: Most popular animal in your country?
qs.a6: Dogs and cats.
qs.a7: Dogs and cats.

qs.q: Wanted a pet as a child? In future?
qs.a6: Yes, I did. In the future, I want a cat, when I have a stable home.
qs.a7: Yes; in future, a cat, once I have a settled home.

qs.q: See many birds and animals where you live?
qs.a6: Yes, there are many birds, chickens and dogs, because it's near the countryside.
qs.a7: Yes, plenty of birds, chickens and dogs, being near the countryside.

qs.q: Been to a zoo?
qs.a6: Yes, Hanoi Zoo with school. I saw elephants and monkeys.
qs.a7: Yes, Hanoi Zoo on a school trip, where I saw elephants and monkeys.

topics.title: Dreams (giấc mơ khi ngủ)

qs.q: Do you often dream? / Do you remember your dreams?
qs.a6: Yes, sometimes. I usually forget them when I wake up, but I remember a few strange ones.
qs.a7: Fairly often. Most fade as soon as I wake up, though a few strange ones stay with me.

qs.q: Do you like talking about your dreams with others?
qs.a6: Sometimes, if the dream is funny. I tell my brother and we laugh together.
qs.a7: Occasionally, when a dream is amusing. I tell my brother and we have a good laugh.

qs.q: Do you think dreams have meanings? / Do you believe dreams can predict the future?
qs.a6: I don't think so. I think dreams come from our thoughts and stress in daily life. But some people believe they have meanings.
qs.a7: Not really. I think they reflect our thoughts and daily stress, although some people do read meaning into them.

qs.q: Have you ever had a bad dream? / What affects the quality of sleep?
qs.a6: Yes, I once dreamed that I was late for an exam. Stress, noise and using the phone before bed can affect our sleep.
qs.a7: Yes, I once dreamt I was late for an exam. Stress, noise and late-night phone use can all disturb sleep.

qs.q: Want to make your dreams come true?
qs.a6: Yes, I mean my dreams about the future, like a good job. I'm working for them.
qs.a7: Yes, my aspirations such as a better career, and I'm working towards them.

qs.q: Do dreams affect life?
qs.a6: Bad dreams can affect my mood in the morning. Good dreams make me happy.
qs.a7: Bad dreams can sour my morning mood, while good ones lift it.

qs.q: Like hearing others' dreams?
qs.a6: Yes, they can be funny and strange.
qs.a7: Yes, they can be funny and bizarre.

topics.title: Food

qs.q: What's your favourite food? / What food do you like to eat?
qs.a6: I like pho and grilled meat with rice. They are delicious and easy to find in Hanoi.
qs.a7: Pho and grilled pork with rice. They're delicious and easy to find in Hanoi.

qs.q: Do you like cooking? / Who cooks in your family?
qs.a6: I can cook simple dishes, but my mother cooks most of the time. I help her wash vegetables.
qs.a7: I can manage simple dishes, but my mother does most of the cooking, and I help with preparation.

qs.q: Do you prefer eating at home or eating out?
qs.a6: At home, because it's cleaner and healthier. But I like eating out with friends at weekends.
qs.a7: At home, as it's healthier and more hygienic, though eating out with friends at weekends is a treat.

qs.q: Is there any food you don't like? / Do you think people eat healthily today?
qs.a6: I don't like very spicy food. I think many people don't eat healthily now, because they eat fast food and sugary drinks.
qs.a7: Very spicy food. I don't think many people eat healthily nowadays, given the popularity of fast food and sugary drinks.

qs.q: Food liked when young? Changed?
qs.a6: When young, I liked fried food and sweets. Now I prefer healthy food, with more vegetables.
qs.a7: As a child I loved fried food and sweets; now I prefer healthier meals with more vegetables.

qs.q: Different foods at different times of the year?
qs.a6: Yes, hot pot in winter and cold desserts in summer. At Tet, we eat banh chung.
qs.a7: Yes, hot pot in winter, cold desserts in summer and banh chung at Tet.

qs.q: Popular food in your country?
qs.a6: Pho, banh mi, rice dishes, noodles and spring rolls.
qs.a7: Pho, banh mi, rice dishes, noodles and spring rolls.

qs.q: Eat with others? Important in your country?
qs.a6: Yes, I like to. In Vietnam, family meals are very important, and eating together shows love.
qs.a7: Yes; in Vietnam, family meals are central, as eating together expresses affection.

topics.title: Sports team

qs.q: Are you a member of a sports team? / Have you ever been in a team?
qs.a6: At school, I was in the football team of my class. Now I only play with colleagues sometimes.
qs.a7: At school I played for my class football team. Nowadays, it's just the occasional game with colleagues.

qs.q: Do you like watching team sports? / Which team do you support?
qs.a6: Yes, I like watching football. I support the Vietnam national team, and I watch with my friends.
qs.a7: Yes, football. I back the Vietnam national team and love watching matches with friends.

qs.q: What are the benefits of joining a sports team?
qs.a6: You can improve your health, make friends and learn teamwork. It's also fun.
qs.a7: It improves fitness, builds friendships and teaches teamwork, and it's fun as well.

qs.q: Is it better to play team sports or individual sports?
qs.a6: For me, team sports are better because they are more fun. But individual sports like swimming are good if you want to exercise at your own time.
qs.a7: I prefer team sports for the fun and camaraderie, although individual sports like swimming suit those who want to exercise at their own pace.

qs.q: Team sports popular?
qs.a6: Yes, football is the most popular. Volleyball and badminton are also common.
qs.a7: Yes, especially football, followed by volleyball and badminton.

qs.q: Is your team famous?
qs.a6: No, it was just a class team.
qs.a7: No, just a class team.

qs.q: Try a new team sport?
qs.a6: Yes, I'd like to try basketball or volleyball.
qs.a7: Yes, basketball or volleyball.

topics.title: Walking

qs.q: Do you like walking? / How often do you walk?
qs.a6: Yes, I do. I walk to the bus stop every day, and sometimes in the evening around my neighbourhood.
qs.a7: Yes. I walk to the bus stop daily and take an evening stroll around my neighbourhood now and then.

qs.q: Where do you like to walk? / Do you walk with others?
qs.a6: I like walking around West Lake because it's cool and beautiful. I walk with friends because we can talk.
qs.a7: Around West Lake, where it's cool and scenic. I like company so that we can chat as we go.

qs.q: Is walking good for health? / Do you think people walk enough now?
qs.a6: Yes, walking is good for the heart and helps us relax. But many people don't walk enough, because they use motorbikes and cars.
qs.a7: Yes, it's good for the heart and the mind. Many people don't walk enough, though, as they rely on motorbikes and cars.

qs.q: Do you prefer walking or other transport for short trips?
qs.a6: For short trips, I prefer walking. It's free and I don't need to find a parking place.
qs.a7: Walking, for short trips. It's free and saves me the hassle of parking.

qs.q: Walk as a child / long walks?
qs.a6: Yes, I walked to school with friends, about 1 km. We rarely took long walks.
qs.a7: Yes, I walked to school with friends, about a kilometre; long walks were rare.

qs.q: Where would you like to take a long walk?
qs.a6: Along the beach in Da Nang, or in the mountains in Sa Pa.
qs.a7: Along Da Nang's beach or through the mountains of Sa Pa.

qs.q: Where did you walk lately?
qs.a6: Around West Lake last Sunday.
qs.a7: Around West Lake last Sunday.

qs.q: How often to the shops?
qs.a6: Almost every day, to the small supermarket near my house.
qs.a7: Almost daily, to the supermarket near my house.

qs.q: Parks near you? Do people enjoy walking in parks?
qs.a6: There's one small park near me. Yes, many people walk there for exercise in the morning and evening.
qs.a7: One small park nearby; yes, many people walk there for exercise morning and evening.
